html:
Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea, was founded in 1827 as Port Clarence, a British naval base on the island of Fernando Po.

Spain had done little with the island, and Britain leased it as a station for the West Africa Squadron, which hunted slave ships in the Gulf of Guinea. Africans freed from captured ships were landed there, and their descendants, the Fernandinos, became a small Creole trading class.

Spain took back control in the 1840s and renamed the town Santa Isabel. It grew as the port for the cocoa plantations of Bioko. In 1973 Macías Nguema gave it its present name, after Malabo, a Bubi king of the early 20th century.
sum: Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea, was founded in 1827 as Port Clarence, a British naval base on the island of Fernando Po.
